'''Kevin Russel Tate''' (8 April 1943 – 22 January 2018) was a New Zealand soil chemist, ecologist and climate scientist.<ref name="retirement">{{cite news |url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1wYz5qh3Xx7wGtVZOGVlmbgWZrn8_x3CR/view |title=Kevin Tate retires |work=Soil News, the newsletter of the New Zealand Soil Society |date=June 2005 | first=Troy | last=Baisden | access-date=28 January 2018}}</ref><ref name="Staff details">{{cite web |url=https://www.landcareresearch.co.nz/about/people/staff-details?id=dGF0ZWs= |title=Kevin Tate – Staff details |publisher=Landcare Research |date=8 June 2012 |access-date=24 January 2018 |archive-date=31 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180131182738/https://www.landcareresearch.co.nz/about/people/staff-details?id=dGF0ZWs= |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Saggar |first1=Surinder and David Whitehead |title=FRSNZ Obituary |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/assets/Uploads/Kevin-Tate-Obituary.pdf |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=13 October 2019}}</ref>

==Early life and family==
Born in [[Lower Hutt]] on 8 April 1943, Tate was the son of Dudley Tate and Hazel Winifred Tate (née Jackson-Hughes).<ref name="Death notice">{{cite news |url=http://deaths.dompost.co.nz/obituaries/dominion-post-nz/obituary.aspx?n=kevin-tate&pid=187944638 |title=Kevin Tate death notice |work=Dominion Post |date=24 January 2018 |access-date=24 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/EP19430409.2.2 | title=Births | date=9 April 1943 | work=Evening Post | access-date=28 January 2018 | page=1}}</ref> He was educated at [[Hutt Valley High School]] from 1956.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.hvhs.school.nz/files/9514/7682/8215/HVHS_Alumni_News_October_2016.pdf | title=The class of '56 celebrates HVHS's 90th anniversary | date=October 2016 | work=Alumni News | access-date=28 January 2018 | first=Robyn | last=Cooper | archive-date=30 January 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180130013044/http://hvhs.school.nz/files/9514/7682/8215/HVHS_Alumni_News_October_2016.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Scientific career==
Tate studied chemistry at [[Victoria University of Wellington]], graduating [[BSc]] in 1964, and [[MSc]] the following year.<ref name="Staff details"/> His master's thesis was titled ''A study of the dealdolisation of diacetone alcohol''.<ref>{{cite web|author=Te Waharoa |url=http://tewaharoa.victoria.ac.nz/VUW:64VUW_ALL:64VUW_INST21136293510002386 |title=A study of the dealdolisation of diacetone alcohol: submitted for the degree of Master of Science in chemistry |publisher=Victoria University of Wellington |access-date=24 January 2018}}</ref> Tate then completed a [[PhD]] on [[decarboxylation]] kinetics and mechanisms under [[Robert Walker Hay]] at Victoria,<ref>{{cite web|author=Te Waharoa |url=http://tewaharoa.victoria.ac.nz/VUW:64VUW_ALL:64VUW_INST21132113060002386 |title=Kinetic and mechanistic studies of decarboxylation: submitted for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy |publisher=Victoria University of Wellington |access-date=24 January 2018}}</ref> before moving to [[Soil Bureau]], a branch of the [[Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (New Zealand)|Department of Scientific and Industrial Research]] (DSIR) in the [[Hutt Valley]]. In 1992, DSIR was dissolved and Soil Bureau became [[Landcare Research]], a [[Crown Research Institute]], and he moved with it to [[Palmerston North]], on the campus of [[Massey University]].

Much of Tate's early research involved the storage and cycling of phosphorus and carbon in soils, particularly in economically important New Zealand grasslands and native forests. Later work focused on [[Carbon cycle|carbon cycling]] and [[Carbon sequestration|sequestration]], particularly as [[Effects of climate change|climate change became an issue]] and the question of how soils and [[soil biota]] could impact atmospheric carbon dioxide levels became relevant.

Tate also contributed his soil chemistry knowledge to other research topics at Soil Bureau / Landcare, including [[sand dune]] rehabilitation, restoration of pasture after [[topsoil]] removal and understanding tussock grasslands. Many papers were coauthored with people including Des J. Ross, C.W. Feltham, Benny K.G. Theng, R.H. Newman, Neal A. Scott, Surinder Saggar, Paul C.D. Newton, Troy Baisden, Aroon Parshotam, [[David A. Wardle]] and [[Gregor W. Yeates]].

Retirement in 2005 did not stop Tate working on his science.<ref name="retirement"/> One of his last works was editing ''Microbial Biomass'', a 2017 volume on soil and ecosystem microbial processes.<ref>{{cite book |title=Microbial biomass |year=2017 |doi=10.1142/q0038 |last1=Tate |first1=Kevin R. |hdl=1983/9a4d9aa8-513d-487c-8007-315a62ced7a1 |isbn=978-1-78634-130-3 |url=https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/en/publications/dynamic-compoundspecific-stable-isotope-probing-of-the-soil-microbial-biomass(9a4d9aa8-513d-487c-8007-315a62ced7a1).html }}</ref>

Tate died in Palmerston North on 22 January 2018.<ref name="Death notice"/>

==Honours and awards==
In 1995, Tate was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]], the peak science organisation in New Zealand.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/all-fellows/s-u/ |title=List of all Fellows with surnames S–U |publisher=Royal Society Te Apārangi |access-date=24 January 2018}}</ref> He was also elected to fellowships of the New Zealand Institute of Chemistry and the New Zealand Society of Soil Science.<ref>{{cite journal |date=24 July 1996 |title=Royal Society of New Zealand Act: election of fellows |url=https://www.gazette.govt.nz/notice/id/1996-gn4955 |journal=New Zealand Gazette |publisher=Department of Internal Affairs |page=1831 |access-date=28 January 2018 |archive-date=28 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128074739/https://www.gazette.govt.nz/notice/id/1996-gn4955 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2005, Tate was awarded the [[Marsden Medal]] by the [[New Zealand Association of Scientists]] for "contribution to, and leadership of, research into ecosystem processes and climate change [spanning] four decades."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scientists.org.nz/awards/marsden-award |title=Marsden Medal |publisher=New Zealand Association of Scientists |access-date=24 January 2018}}</ref>
